title: Derived completeness of supported kernels and images of integral scalar local models
statement:
Let $X$ be an affine scheme [def-pc-scheme]. Use the small étale and pro-étale sites in the small indexing universe [def-weil-pbc-etale-site, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-size-convention]. A support chain over $X$ means a finite chain $S=T_r\xrightarrow{a_r}\cdots\xrightarrow{a_1}T_0=X$, where each arrow is a quasi-compact open immersion or a closed immersion with quasi-compact open complement [def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-closed-immersion, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. For a condensed coefficient ring $R$, put $R_T=p_T^*R$ and $\mathcal A_{R,T}=\operatorname{Mod}_{R_T}$. Write $J_R=J_{R,1}\circ\cdots\circ J_{R,r}$, where $J_{R,t}=(a_t)_!$ in the open case and $J_{R,t}=(a_t)_*$ in the closed case [def-sfb-module-open-lower-shriek, def-sfb-module-lower-star]. For an affine pro-étale object $v:U\to X$, set $F_{R,v}=v^*J_R$. The empty chain has $J_R=\mathrm{id}$. All derived categories and $R\Gamma$ are the ordinary uncompleted module-derived ones, with section complexes valued in abelian groups [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull].

Fix a prime $\ell$. For a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, let $B=\mathcal O_E$ with its norm topology and let $\pi$ be a uniformizer [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Write $B_T=p_T^*C(-,B)$ and $k_{n,T}=(B/\pi^n)_T$, with the finite discrete coefficients, for $n\geq1$ [sk-def-localizing-closure]. The case $E=\mathbf Q_\ell$ gives $B=\mathbf Z_\ell$.

A finite scalar local model means a module which on a pro-étale cover has the form $R_T\otimes_{\underline{R(*)}}\underline P$, where $P$ is a finitely presented scalar $R(*)$-module, that is, a cokernel of a map between finite free scalar modules [sk-def-sfb-constructible]. The scalar modules and covers may differ for different terms. For any actual module map $f:L\to M$ between such modules on $S$, write $I_f=\operatorname{im}f$ in the abelian module category, not the closure of a topological image.

For every such integral map $f$, the degree-zero complexes of $\ker f$ and $\operatorname{im}f$ on $S$ are derived $\pi$-complete. Their actual supported restrictions $F_{B,v}(\ker f)[0]$ and $F_{B,v}(\operatorname{im}f)[0]$ are also derived $\pi$-complete for every support chain and every affine pro-étale $v:U\to X$. Explicitly, for each of these complexes $K$ on its scheme $T$, the specified quotient-tower completion unit is an isomorphism in the ordinary category $D(\operatorname{Mod}(B_T))$:
$$K\xrightarrow{\sim}R\varprojlim_{n\geq1}\operatorname{Res}_{B_T\to k_{n,T}}(K\otimes^L_{B_T}k_{n,T}).$$
Derived completeness and the normalized quotient tower have the meaning of [sk-def-pe-derived-completion]. No torsion cohomological-dimension hypothesis or vanishing conclusion is imposed; ordinary images, nonconstant maps, torsion scalar models, the zero map, the identity and empty chains are included.

source.place: Lemma 3.4.14 (kernels, cokernels and images of derived complete modules), Proposition 3.5.1 and Definition 3.5.2 (completed coefficients); HRS Section 7.1.1 for local models. Agent supported kernel/image specialization. Exact reference for preservation by the specified support chain is WANTED.

proof.text: Apply supported_kernel_image_base_complete to the actual morphism f and the two finite scalar local model hypotheses, obtaining completeness of kernel f and image f on S.

Apply supported_extension_derived_complete separately to kernel f and image f, using their source completeness and the actual finite path p and site object U. Pair these two results with the two source conclusions to obtain the four conjuncts.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q25-cd012157e (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, the new node, every cited statement and the sources in full. The item's statement and stmt_deps are identical to live; live has the item unsplit with no repair note, so the delivery is not superseded. The item's closure is acyclic. Step 1: lem-sfb-finite-scalar-local-model-complete matches the item's hypothesis exactly (same B_T = p_T^*C(-,O_E), torsion allowed). Step 2: the exact section-ring equivalence and its unit comparison, plus the det-pe-derived-nakayama exact sequence, give π regular on R with E(k_n) = R/π^nR, so the new node applies with t = π. Step 3: localization (closed i with quasi-compact complementary open j, joint detection), the restriction comparison of the completion unit, and the exactness clause of the recollement node (on route via sk-thm-properbasechange) together give completeness after one support arrow. Step 4 is an induction with the claim, base and step all stated. Step 5 uses the site-object clause of the comparison node. New node lem-sfb-principal-complete-heart-kernels: I checked it against BS 1309.1198 Lemma 3.4.14 (p.23) together with Props. 3.1.9 and 4.2.8. The telescope argument holds: T_t(coker) ≅ T_t(ker)[2], with amplitudes [0,1] and [-2,-1], so both vanish. Small cases (g = 0, identity, t a unit, R = 0, t-torsion modules) are fine. The node makes no claim about arbitrary submodules, is statement-only and self-contained, and is a strictly smaller general lemma, not a clause of the item. Duplicate search: lem-weil-pbc-torsion-limit-sheaf-completeness uses the discrete constant Noetherian ring and an RHom definition of completeness, so it is not a duplicate; sk-lem-int-integral-heart, complete-integral-residue-functor and condensed-constructible-serre also differ. I accept the declared tool uses as generic or on route. lean.statement:
theorem supported_kernel_image_derived_complete
    (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (E : Type u) [Field E]
    [Algebra (Padic l) E] [FiniteDimensional (Padic l) E]
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsAffine X]
    {S : Scheme.{u}} (tree : QcqsOpenClosedTree X) (p : tree.Path S)
    (L M : AdicCompletion.Modules l E S) (f : L ⟶ M)
    (hL : HasFiniteConstantLocalModel (DerivedNakayama.integerRing l E) S L)
    (hM : HasFiniteConstantLocalModel (DerivedNakayama.integerRing l E) S M)
    (U : X.ProEt) [IsAffine U.left] :
    IsDerivedComplete l E S ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor _ 0).obj (kernel f)) ∧
    IsDerivedComplete l E S ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor _ 0).obj (image f)) ∧
    IsDerivedComplete l E U.left ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor _ 0).obj
      ((CondensedRing.upperStar (DerivedNakayama.integerRing l E) U.hom).obj
        ((p.extension (DerivedNakayama.integerRing l E)).obj (kernel f)))) ∧
    IsDerivedComplete l E U.left ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor _ 0).obj
      ((CondensedRing.upperStar (DerivedNakayama.integerRing l E) U.hom).obj
        ((p.extension (DerivedNakayama.integerRing l E)).obj (image f))))
lean.note: Uses the existing QcqsOpenClosedTree.Path and its actual extension functor to encode all allowed finite support chains over the affine base. Complementary siblings may be leaves; the root path is the empty chain. The four conjuncts are source kernel/image completeness and their supported affine pro-etale restrictions, using the recorded IsDerivedComplete predicate.

reviewed_lean.note: Item changes only in its lean record and one new stmt_dep, def-sfb-qcqs-open-closed-tree, which is landed (allowed); all other nodes identical to side-live; statement matches file verbatim. QcqsOpenClosedTree.Path.extension encodes exactly the allowed support chains over affine X: qcqs vertices, complements as possibly single-vertex siblings, any open/closed immersion, root = empty chain = identity. HasFiniteConstantLocalModel gives separate covers and finitely presented scalar modules, torsion allowed, same predicate as finite_scalar_local_model_complete. kernel f and image f are the abelian kernel and image. The four conjuncts are completeness on S and of upperStar U.hom after p.extension, U affine, using the recorded IsDerivedComplete (K-flat Roos augmentation, ordinary derived category). No added hypotheses or universe restrictions; edge cases covered. Docstrings carry source, blueprint tag and 5 proof steps; proof is sorry only; report has both sections.
